exposure: Placental lesions (maternal/fetal vascular supply lesions, maternal/fetal inflammatory responses)
outcome: Composite adverse neonatal outcome (sepsis, transfusion, phototherapy, respiratory morbidity, cerebral morbidity, NEC, or death)
cohort: The study included pregnant women diagnosed with preeclampsia between 2008 and 2016.
finding: Preeclampsia with severe features was associated with more pronounced placental pathology, particularly maternal vascular malperfusion lesions, and a higher rate of adverse neonatal outcomes compared to mild preeclampsia.
gest_age: Lower gestational age at delivery in the severe PE group (p<0.001)
